hypothesis: A software cycle of the PMIC switch DC1SW2 resets the microSD card without losing the PMIC link or the FEL link.
prediction:
Source analysis, no board run. The card's VDD is the net VCC-CARD through R51 (1 ohm), with C236 and C237 (100 nF, 10 uF) at the socket (schematic sheet 12). No load switch or GPIO gates it: the commented card-pwr-gpios property (sun60i-a733-orangepi-zero3w.dts:1630) has no hardware behind it. The PMIC (AXP8191, address 0x36; the drawing calls it AXP318) enables DC1SW2 with register 0x11 bit 4 (AXP8191_DCDC_CTL2); its voltage is the shared DCDC1 selector at 0x12. DC1SW2 is enabled (0x11 reads 0x17; DC1SW1 is off).
Three sources, for which net each rail name is on:
| Source | VCC-CARD | VCC-IO | VCC-PL (PMIC I2C pads) | USB0 supply VCC33-USB | VCC-PE |
| Sheet 2, power sequence | DC1SW2 | DC1SW2 | ALDO1 | ALDO1 | BLDO1 |
| Vendor device tree | DC1SW2 (vmmc-supply, dts:1646) | not stated | not stated | not stated | BLDO1 (dts:3628) |
| Sheet 6, the PMIC drawing | DCDC1 itself (alias stub under DCDC1) | DC1SW2 (SWOUT2 stub) | DC1SW2 | DC1SW2 | DC1SW2 |
Sheet 6 lists rail names on each PMIC output as stubs. Its SWOUT2 group holds VCC33-18-USB, VCC33-USB, VCC33-18-USB-2, VCC33-USB-2, VCC-PD, VCC-PL, VCC-IO and VCC-PE; its DCDC1 group holds VCC-3V3-WIFI, VCC_3V3_EXT, VCC_3V3_CSI, VCC-CARD, VCC_3V3_EMMC and VCC-LCD. Sheet 2 and the vendor tree agree and not with that drawing. The stub list on sheet 6 contradicts itself: it puts PD, PL, IO and PE, which sheet 2 gives four different outputs (BLDO2, ALDO1, DC1SW2, BLDO1, two at 1.8 V and two at 3.3 V), on one net. An earlier note (docs/pcie.md) read the same stub group as BLDO1. Sheet 6 is read as unreliable for this question and sheet 2 plus the vendor tree as likely, but nothing in the documents settles it; the only physical check is the rail itself.
Readings of a DC1SW2 cycle. Sheet 2 and the vendor tree right: DC1SW2 powers the card, so a cycle can reset it; it also drops VCC-IO (the PB bank, the FEL and JTAG-SEL pads, WREQIN), VCC-PH, the USB2 host PHY supplies, the 3.3 V header rail, the fan and eMMC. Sheet 6 right: the card is on DCDC1 and does not lose power; the cycle does nothing for the card, and it drops the supply of the PMIC's own I2C pads (VCC-PL: S_TWI0 pins PL0 and PL1), the USB0 and USB2 analog supplies, and VCC-IO, VCC-PD and VCC-PE; with the I2C pads unpowered software cannot re-enable the rail, and with USB0 unpowered the FEL link is gone, so the board would need power removal.
Consumers when DC1SW2 drops:
| Consumer (net) | What it is on this board | Effect of the drop | Source |
| VCC-CARD, the socket | the microSD card | card loses VDD; resets once VDD is below 0.5 V for 1 ms | sheets 2, 12; vendor tree |
| SoC VCC-IO: PB0-PB10 | UART0 on PB9 and PB10 (console header), I2S0, TWI0, TWI1 on PB pins | pins lose their supply; UART0 and the header GPIOs go dead; the runner does not use them (FEL is over USB0) | datasheet pin table 2311-2343; sheet 9 |
| SoC VCC-IO: FEL pad (1W1), JTAG-SEL (1W2), WREQIN (1T24) | boot strap inputs with pull-ups from VCC-IO | with VCC-IO off the FEL pad no longer reads its pulled-up value; the ROM selects FEL on four low samples, so a reset during the off time is benign | datasheet 3305-3307, 2280; boot-rom-and-boot0.md |
| SoC VCC-IO: PF0-PF6 | SDC0 and card detect, supplied from VCC-IO or VCC18-PF by the adaptive selector | the bank follows CLDO5 (1.8 V) while VCC-IO is off, so the card's pins see 1.8 V logic while its supply is off | datasheet 2535-2561; sd-uhs.md |
| SoC VCC-PH | PH0-PH16, including BOARD-ID-SEL-GPIO (PH15) and DDR-PARA-SEL-GPIO (PH16) | pins unpowered; only boot0 reads the two straps, not our FEL path | sheet 9 |
| USB2 PHY (VCC-USB-2, VCC33-18-USB-2) | the USB host port (webcam, serial, radio when on USB) | the host link drops and devices re-enumerate on return; the OS's USB2 task must be idle | sheets 2, 6 |
| 3.3 V header, VCC-SENSOR, VCC-3V3 | the 40-pin header supply and the SoC sensor supply (also fed by CLDO5 per sheet 2) | header devices lose power | sheet 2 |
| Fan (fan-supply, PWM on PD5) | cooling fan | stops; the thermal controller must not rely on it during the hold | dts:1531 |
| VCC-eMMC | no eMMC fitted | none | handoff |
| TWI pull-ups (twi-supply), GMAC 3.3 V | TWI5 and TWI12 nodes (disabled) and GMAC0 (disabled) | none | dts:1864, 1942, 3314 |
| Under sheet 6 only: VCC-PL, VCC33-USB, VCC-PD, VCC-PE | PMIC I2C pads, USB0 analog, PD and PE banks | PMIC link and FEL link lost | sheet 6 |
The PMIC interrupt (PMU-IRQ) and bus (PMU-SDA, PMU-SCK) are on PL pins, so their safety depends on which output VCC-PL is on (ALDO1 by sheet 2, DC1SW2 by sheet 6). The watchdog is inside the SoC and uses no pad. The runner uses USB0 only.
Whether the board comes back. Hold and re-enable need the PMIC link: the cycle writes register 0x11 over S_TWI0 on PL0 and PL1; if VCC-PL is on ALDO1 the link is untouched, if on DC1SW2 the write cannot reach the PMIC. A reset during the hold: the PMIC keeps its rail registers across a watchdog reset (the CPU rails do), so DC1SW2 would stay off; the ROM then runs its FEL sample on a pad whose supply is off (reads as FEL), and the FEL path needs only USB0 (ALDO1 by sheet 2, DC1SW2 by sheet 6). Under sheet 2 the runner reaches FEL and the next image re-enables the rail (the rail normalisation would need the DC1SW2 bit added); under sheet 6 it does not. The FEL pad and the PF bank (the ROM's SD probe) depend on VCC-IO and both fail safe (FEL on a low pad; a failed probe falls to FEL); DRAM, the CPU rails and the PMIC link do not depend on it by sheet 2. The risk that the board does not return is the sheet 6 risk, which the documents cannot exclude.
Hold time. The card side has 10.1 uF at the socket; the SoC's VCC-IO, VCC-PH, VCC-PD, VCC-PE and VCC-PL pins each have 100 nF to 1 uF and one 10 uF part (C183 to C197, about 12 uF); the USB supply pins have four pairs of 1 uF and 100 nF (about 5 uF); the header, sensor and fan supplies are not drawn with values: a total of 30 to 50 uF. No active discharge is known (the PMIC's switch pull-down bit is not in the sources). The card's idle current (about 0.2 to 1 mA at 3.3 V, falling as VDD falls) is the largest known load, an effective resistance of 3 to 16 kohm; with 40 uF the time constant is 0.13 to 0.65 s, and falling from 3.3 V to 0.5 V takes 1.9 time constants: 0.25 to 1.2 s. Leakage only slows the tail. A 300 ms hold is below the likely time with no margin; a hold of 3 s would cover the range and is checked by the card resetting, not assumed.
conclusion: Not run. The nets that DC1SW2 powers are unsettled between the schematic sheets, so no DC1SW2 cycle is planned; the discharge time is an estimate, with no board measurement behind it.
narrative: Documents read: schematic V1.2 sheets 2, 6, 9 and 12, the vendor device tree and the A733 datasheet pin tables; no measurement of any rail was made.

hypothesis: The session-start resolution algorithm ends every cut session usable at the card level, sending no command at 1.8 V to a card signalling 3.3 V.
narrative: Host model only (checks/sd-uhs-recovery-model.py). The model cuts a session after every step of the switch lifetime (CMD0 through the reads), for both unknowns (what a card already at 1.8 V answers to ACMD41 with S18R, and whether a 3.3 V host reads such a card), for a reset that restores the bank to 3.3 V and one that does not, and for a session that ends with the bank restored or left at 1.8 V, and starts the resolution algorithm below each time. All 256 sessions end usable at the card's own level, with no command sent at 1.8 V to a card signalling 3.3 V. A card without UHS-I stays at 3.3 V. A stuck card is left unresolved by the algorithm and cleared by the supply-cycle model once the hold exceeds the discharge time, as expected. Replacing the 1.8 V probe or probing at 1.8 V first makes the check fail. With the close added as the last two steps, all 144 sessions (every cut x both unknowns x both reset behaviours) end usable. checks/sd-return-close.py --lifetimes (605 cuts over the lifetimes 1 and 2; 2,868 cuts including the SDR104 lifetime at 150 MHz, 100 MHz and with no window, with a cut at every poll except every 9th inside the sweep) shows at every cut no command with the bank at 1.8 V and the card at 3.3 V, agreement of selector, platform record and card level, and at most one write to each level; the mutations that skip the restore write or send CMD11 in re-entry fail it.

hypothesis: The core's CMD19 tuning sweep ends in the window decision, or in a terminal fault only for a failure that is not a sampling effect, for every injected fault.
prediction:
Audit of the sweep against the vendor loop, done after the first three board submissions of the request-pattern experiment each stopped in the sweep on a different check that fired on a marginal delay. Each fix had added a tolerated bit or an exemption, and each time the host model lacked the board's failure kind. The coordinator's rule is a full diff against the reference before a board run.
Reference: sunxi_mmc_execute_tuning in the board kernel (bsp/drivers/mmc/sunxi-mmc.c:2432-2640), sunxi_mmc_clk_gating_reset (:227), sunxi_mmc_reset_host (:640), the v4p5x __sunxi_mmc_do_oclk_onoff and sunxi_mmc_save_spec_reg_v4p5x. The vendor loop, for each of the 64 delays: reset the host (save the registers, gate the bus clock off and on through the CCU, restore the saved registers), update the clock with oclk_en(1), write the sample delay, then issue CMD19 up to 20 times, stopping at the first error or pattern mismatch; the delay passes if all 20 matched. After the loop it picks the best delay, resets the host once more, writes it, and resets and updates the clock a last time. It never waits for the command or data state machine, never sends CMD12, and does not reset the FIFO separately. It judges a delay by cmd.error || data.error || memcmp(pattern) (:2561-2576) and nothing else: no R1 status, FIFO or controller state, or register verification. cmd.error and data.error are set by sunxi_mmc_finalize_request (:1060-1100) when any bit of SDXC_INTERRUPT_ERROR_BIT (sunxi-mmc.h:215-218: bits 1, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15) is in the interrupt sum, and by the transfer watchdog (sunxi_timerout_handle, :270-310, SUNXI_TRANS_TIMEOUT 5 s, :87) for a request that neither completes nor errors.
| Step | Vendor | Core before the audit | Core after | Kept or changed, and why |
| Repeats per delay, stop at first failure, pattern compare, window rule (first longest run, 12 or more, midpoint) | 20; yes; yes; yes | the same | the same | kept: identical |
| Reset before a delay | every delay, passing or failing | only after a failed command | only after a failed command | kept: a passing command leaves the controller idle; a reset before each of 64 delays adds 64 register restores, each with its own failure modes, and nothing shows a benefit |
| Wait for the command or data state machine before the reset | none | up to 10 ms, then (first fix) a forced reset | none: reset at once | changed: this was the timing-dependent difference |
| Reset mechanism | CCU bus gate and reset toggle plus register save and restore | GCTRL soft, FIFO and DMA reset (|7), then rewrite of the SDR104 registers | the same GCTRL reset (the value of the vendor's sunxi_mmc_reset_host) and the same rewrite | kept: the CCU toggle belongs to the platform (the bus register has its own filter rules) and needs a new platform operation; if a stuck command survives the GCTRL reset the cap below trips and it becomes the next step |
| Registers restored | GCTRL, CLKCR, TMOUT, WIDTH, FTRGL, FUNS, DBGC, DMAC, DLBA, IMASK; DRV_DL, SAMP_DL, DS_DL, NTSR, EDSD, CSDC | drive phase (0x140), NTSR (0x5c), sample delay, TMOUT, WIDTH, CLKCR | the same | kept: the sweep is PIO with the interrupt masked, so GCTRL, FTRGL, DMAC, DLBA and IMASK do not take part; the SDR104 ones are rewritten and read back |
| Clock update after the reset | oclk_en(1): CLKCR clock on, low power on (power-save mode), DAT0 masked; update command; wait; clear the interrupt flags; clear the mask | clock on only, update command, no mask | clock on with DAT0 masked, update command, clear the flags, clear the mask, read back | changed: a card that still holds DAT0 low stalls an update that does not mask it |
| Low-power clock gating | on (the board's device tree sets sunxi-power-save-mode) | off | off | kept: the vendor's own comment for this chip says it wants the clock always on to avoid a sample bug, and our delays were derived with it on |
| Delay change | write SAMP_DL after the clock update, clock running | same, without a clock stop | same | kept: identical in effect |
| Data timeout of CMD19 | the host's default | TMOUT 0x040000ff (about 1.7 ms at 150 MHz) | the same | kept: it bounds a command that gets no data |
| CMD12 or abort | none | none | none | identical |
| FIFO reset | none separate (the bus reset clears it) | within the GCTRL reset | within the GCTRL reset | kept: a superset |
| Reset after the sweep | reset, write the best delay, update the clock | write the best delay, restore the timeout | the same | kept: when the last delay failed the recovery has just reset; when it passed there is nothing to reset |
| Cap on trouble | none | none | consecutive recoveries that do not complete within 10 ms (reset bits still set, or the update still pending): the reset is repeated and after 12 in a row the sweep stops with TIMEOUT; a completed recovery clears the count | added |
Host evidence for the recovery change: the card model has a failing delay that leaves the command stuck and DAT0 low: the old recovery (wait, then reset) timed out as the board did; the new one resets at once, completes the masked update and finishes the sweep with the same window; a controller that stays stuck through reset and update makes the sweep stop with TIMEOUT after 12 recoveries; removing the mask from the update makes the stuck-DAT0 case fail.
The rule written down by the audit: while a CMD19 is in flight, any failure the attempt can produce fails that delay and never ends the sweep. It is one function, fault() in sunxi_mmc.c: while tune_attempt is set (set when the CMD19 is queued, cleared when the P_SD_TUNE step judges it), a CONTROLLER or CARD error becomes tune_failed, which starts the recovery that resets the controller and moves to the next delay. The earlier list of tolerated interrupt bits (TUNE_TOLERATED) is gone. An attempt with no completion and no error within 10 ms (TUNE_ATTEMPT_US, the vendor's watchdog scaled to this driver) fails its delay too. The R1 status of the CMD19 is not judged, as in the vendor loop. Paths that stay terminal, through fatal() (the old fault()):
| Path (function, check) | Vendor | Ours | Why |
| rd, wr, fence, FIFO read: a callback fails | not applicable (MMIO cannot fail) | terminal IO | the platform adapter refused the access (a filter or lease failure), not a sampling effect |
| time_ok: clock backwards, operation deadline | none | terminal TIME, TIMEOUT | the caller's own limits |
| poll: ownership lost (retained) | none | terminal ADMISSION | the bank and clock are no longer ours |
| interrupts: card remove (bit 31) or the controller's bit 18 | removal handled by the card-detect path | terminal CONTROLLER | the card is gone; nothing to tune |
| Attempts that hang, TUNE_HUNG_CAP (12) in a row | the 5 s watchdog, no cap | terminal TIMEOUT after 12 consecutive hung attempts | a card or controller that never answers; a completed attempt, passing or failing, clears the count |
| tune_recover: the reset bits stay set or the clock update stays pending | none (the reset is a clock gate toggle) | the reset repeats; after TUNE_FORCED_RESETS (12) consecutive incomplete recoveries, terminal TIMEOUT | |
| tune_recover: GCTRL lost its CPU-FIFO bit after the reset, or the restored registers read back wrong | none (the vendor restores without reading back) | terminal CONTROLLER | the recovery's own checks, not the attempt's; a controller that cannot be restored cannot sample |
| set_delay: the delay register reads back wrong | none | terminal CONTROLLER | same |
Paths that became attempt failures (all through fault()): the command or data start bit still set at issue (command_step step 0), the control register's FIFO or DMA state not as the PIO command needs (step 1), every error bit in the interrupt register (interrupts, in steps 0, 2 and 3), the FIFO not empty after the block (step 3), and the R1 card-error faults of command_step and card_response (the R1 check at the data command is skipped in a sweep). The DMA status faults and the IDMAC steps 4 to 6 do not run for CMD19, which is PIO. A busy or start bit that never clears has no error, and the attempt timer ends it. Host fuzz (checks/sunxi-mmc-uhs.c, function fuzz) injects one fault per sweep with the model's inj_* fields, armed before attempt 0 of each delay and before attempt 19 of four delays inside the window: every interrupt bit, every R1 status bit, every bit of the status register (kept until a reset), every bit of the control register (one read, after the resets are done; bits 0 to 2 excluded because flipping a reset-in-progress bit only makes software proceed early), all bits at once, a command that never completes with the start bit clear and with it set. A run passes when the sweep ends READY with a window or the no-window fallback. The removal bits (18 and 31) must fault.
conclusion:
